issues.issue: The provision sets two different triggers — the Agreement is "conditioned upon commencement of your employment" by April 16, 2012 and "void" if employment does not begin, yet is "effective upon the first date that all the parties have signed" — leaving the operative date and the condition's effect uncertain.

"You are expected to complete satisfactorily all assignments and training obligations" is hortatory rather than promissory, and "satisfactorily" is measured only by Wells Fargo's "sole discretion"; whether this creates an enforceable duty is arguable.
"At least initially, you will be eligible for overtime pay" fixes no end point for overtime eligibility, and the phrase "at least initially" is open-ended on its face.

The promise that compensation is paid "in accordance with" the New FA Compensation Plan sits against Paragraph 8's statement that the Agreement is only a "synopsis" of compensation arrangements and that plans may be changed unilaterally, so it is unclear which document governs pay.

The overtime cut-off is tied to the title change, but the trigger requires both licence attainment and "graduation from the Training Program", leaving the moment eligibility ends open where those events do not coincide.

It ends overtime eligibility on a title change, while Paragraph 3 says overtime eligibility applies "at least initially" and Paragraph 10(b)(i) treats graduation and full registration as separate milestones; the milestones are not aligned across the instrument.

"May lead to consequences, up to and including termination from the Training Program" states no determinate consequence, and "your test dates will extended" is missing a verb; both leave the effect of a failed exam indeterminate.

The enumerated prohibitions (i)-(iv) on beneficiary designations, fiduciary appointments, powers of attorney and bequests are introduced by "including without limitation" language about internal policies, so whether the list is exhaustive of prohibited client benefits is arguable.

The statement that this Agreement "does not supersede or replace, in part or whole, any provisions of the Wells Fargo human resources policies and programs" cannot be squared with Paragraph 20's declaration that the Agreement is "the entire understanding" between the parties.

The at-will statement that "You are not hired for any specified term or duration pursuant to a contract of employment" is in tension with Paragraph 10(b)(i), which conditions forgiveness of Training Costs on five years' "continuous employment", and with Paragraph 8's description of the document as a mere "synopsis".
"This Agreement serves only as a synopsis of the compensation and other arrangements" is ambiguous as to whether the document creates binding obligations or merely summarises terms found elsewhere.

Calling the document only a "synopsis" of arrangements in effect elsewhere contradicts Paragraph 20, which states that "This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between you and Wells Fargo Advisors".

The proviso excepting "any Wells Fargo Advisors compensation or benefit plans or policies" from the written-modification requirement swallows much of the rule, since the substance of the Agreement is compensation; the boundary of the carve-out is uncertain.

"Wells Fargo Advisors shall be liable to you only for compensation earned and received by Wells Fargo Advisors" is opaque about whose earning and receipt matters, and "deficit balances (unrelated to the offset of the draw)" is undefined.

The unlimited recovery of "fronted" or advanced amounts on termination "for any reason whatsoever" sits uneasily with Paragraph 3's promise of a bi-weekly salary and overtime pay, which the setoff could absorb.
Employment is required both "on the date such payments are received by Wells Fargo Advisors" and "on the applicable payout date"; the two conditions are stated as one but are different dates.

The forfeiture of "any revenue or fees" on termination is hard to reconcile with Paragraph 9(a), which preserves liability for "salary earned but not yet paid to you prior to the effective date of the termination".

The obligation to reimburse arises if employment "is terminated for any reason at any time", which on its face includes termination by Wells Fargo without cause, and the dollar amounts referenced as "set forth below" are illegible/blank in the instrument.

The blanket "for any reason at any time" reimbursement duty must be read against the exceptions in Paragraph 10(b) and the amortisation in Paragraph 10(c), which measure the repayment window from different starting events.
"Continuous employment" is undefined, and the five-year clock runs from the later of graduation or full registration without addressing leave, transfer or breaks in service.

The five-year forgiveness period runs from graduation/registration, while Paragraph 10(c) amortises the same Training Costs over forty-eight months beginning in the second year of employment as a New FA; the two schedules do not end at the same time.

"Competitive Organization or Entity" is defined by a list of financial firms followed by the catch-all "any other person, firm, corporation, or entity that competes with Wells Fargo Advisors", so the reach of the catch-all beyond the enumerated categories is genuinely uncertain (and the phrase "including, but not be limited to" is ungrammatical).

This exception operates as a de facto one-year non-compete, which cannot easily be squared with Paragraph 12, whose post-employment restrictions are limited to non-solicitation of clients and employees.

It is unclear whether the reimbursable amount is reduced by 1/48 of the total cumulatively each month or whether some other reduction is meant, and "the first month of the second year after your have begun employment" is garbled as to the start date.

A forty-eight-month amortisation beginning in the second year of New FA employment cannot be reconciled with Paragraph 10(b)(i)'s five-year forgiveness period measured from graduation and full registration; an employee could owe nothing under one and still owe under the other.

Setting off Training Costs against "monthly compensation" presupposes the monthly compensation structure of Paragraph 4, which applies only after graduation, leaving the mechanism unclear for a New FA paid a bi-weekly salary under Paragraph 3.

The definition sweeps in "All records and other documents made and/or maintained in connection with Wells Fargo Advisors business" and "All information contained in or derived from" them, without limitation to confidential material, so the boundary of the enumerated list against the catch-all is contestable.

The surrender obligation applies to "Confidential Records or Documents", a term that appears nowhere else and does not match the defined "Confidential Information and Documents" in Paragraph 11(a); the scope of what must be returned is therefore uncertain.
The restriction covers any client "that you had contact with or otherwise learned of" during employment, and "otherwise learned of" has no discernible outer boundary.

The sentence breaks grammatically at "or discontinuing his or her employment", which has no subject or verb tying it to the prohibited solicitation, and the catch-all "any other lines of business in which Wells Fargo Advisors or any of its affiliates is engaged" is boundless after the specific list.

"You will be expected to contribute" states an expectation rather than an obligation, and the amount is "determined after a consultation" with management without any standard, so both the duty and its measure are indeterminate.

"You will be accountable for errors" does not say what accountability means financially, and "trading errors that may have a financial impact on future earnings" is an unclear qualifier on the disciplinary exposure.
"Net Eligible Revenue" is capitalised as a defined term but is defined nowhere in this Agreement, only in the extrinsic New FA Compensation Plan.

The adjustment operates through "monthly compensation under the New FA Compensation Plan", which under Paragraph 4 only begins after graduation, leaving no mechanism for a salaried New FA under Paragraph 3.

The disclosure describes arbitration of "any dispute, claim or controversy that may arise between you and Wells Fargo Advisors, or a client, or any other person", and the catch-all "any other person" has no discernible limit.

This description of the scope of arbitration is broader than the operative clause in Paragraph 14(b), which covers only controversies "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors", so the summary and the operative term point in different directions.

The statement that statutory discrimination claims "IS REQUIRED to be arbitrated" sits against Paragraph 14(a)(4), which preserves the right to file agency charges, and against Paragraph 14(b), which lists discrimination among arbitrable claims without the exclusions stated in 14(a)(3).

The exclusion is for "claims for State unemployment insurance", but the "i.e." list that follows includes workers' compensation and "claims under the National Labor Relations Act", which are not State unemployment insurance; the category and its illustrations do not match.

These exclusions appear only in the explanatory Paragraph 14(a), whereas the operative arbitration clause in Paragraph 14(b) says "Except as provided in Paragraph 14(c)" and carries no such carve-outs, leaving it uncertain whether the exclusions are operative.

The preservation of agency charges followed by automatic arbitration "upon receipt of a right to sue letter or similar administrative determination" is in tension with Paragraph 14(a)(3), which excludes certain administratively processed claims from arbitration altogether.
The clause reads "the rules of the arbitration forum in the claim is filed", omitting a word ("in which"), which garbles the reference to the forum whose rules govern panel composition.

The statement that "a claim that is ineligible for arbitration may be brought to court" is in tension with Paragraph 14(b)'s directive that claims FINRA does not accept go instead to the American Arbitration Association.

The clause lists specific claim types and closes with "and/or other theory", a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is uncertain, and it is limited to disputes "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors" without any "arising out of employment" limitation.
Paragraph 14(b) excepts only Paragraph 14(c) and so appears to compel arbitration of the very claims Paragraph 14(a)(3) says are "specifically EXCLUDED from this obligation to arbitrate".

The carve-out from arbitration runs one way only — Wells Fargo alone may seek court relief "[n]otwithstanding any other provision" — which is the kind of one-sided drafting that invites construction against the drafter.

The survival list expressly preserves "indemnification obligations", but the Agreement contains no indemnification provision — Paragraph 13 imposes only a contribution expectation — so the reference cannot be matched to any operative term.

Missouri law is chosen for an agreement made for a New York branch employee whose restrictive covenants in Paragraphs 11 and 12 would ordinarily be tested under New York law; nothing else in the instrument addresses that mismatch.

The fallback says invalidity "shall not affect the validity or unenforceability of the remaining Provisions", which as written preserves their unenforceability — plainly a drafting slip inverting the intended sense.
The clause preserves rights only as to "any other breach of the same or any other covenant", which by negative implication suggests that forbearance does waive the individual breach forgone.

The paragraph is headed "RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS" and acknowledges covenants "IN THEIR ENTIRETY", yet contains none itself and Paragraph 17 says captions "shall not affect in any way the meaning or interpretation", leaving which provisions are the acknowledged restrictive covenants unsettled.
The integration is qualified by "regarding the matters addressed herein", a limitation whose scope is itself indeterminate.

The declaration of an entire understanding cannot be squared with Paragraph 8, which says the Agreement "serves only as a synopsis", or with Paragraph 6, which says it "does not supersede or replace" Wells Fargo's human resources policies and compliance guidelines.
"All provisions ... that require survival ... in order to give full legal effect thereto" is circular: it identifies the surviving provisions only by reference to their own need to survive.
This open-ended survival rule overlaps with Paragraph 15, which already specifies which terms survive termination, leaving it unclear whether Paragraph 15's list is exhaustive.
